children: Shares in Tower Semiconductor rose Thursday after it said it has begun high-volume shipments with NewPhotonics of laser-integrated optical chips made for artificial intelligence infrastructure.
The Israel-based companies on Thursday said co-developed chips were designed to meet urgent and growing demand for high-bandwidth, energy-efficient optical interconnects in AI servers.
The initial shipments support data rates of 800G to 1.6T, with higher capacity 6.4T versions scheduled for the first half of next year.

"By combining our optical chip design with [Tower's] manufacturing platform, we are first to bring higher-bandwidth, energy-efficient highly integrated systems to the OEM customer and data center market," Senior Vice President and General Manager of NewPhotonics Doron Tal said.
